stem: Which substance is synthesised by human tissues?
rationale: Normal human tissues can synthesize purines and pyrimidines from amphibolic intermediates.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > PURINES & PYRIMIDINES ARE DIETARILY NONESSENTIAL

stem: Mononucleotides are converted into which substance?
rationale: The resulting mononucleotides from their degradation in the intestinal tract may be absorbed or converted to purine and pyrimidine bases.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > PURINES & PYRIMIDINES ARE DIETARILY NONESSENTIAL

stem: ATP is converted into which substance?
rationale: ATP is used to convert AMP and GMP to ADP and GDP, respectively. Conversion of GDP to GTP involves an additional phosphoryl transfer from ATP.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > INOSINE MONOPHOSPHATE (IMP) IS SYNTHESIZED FROM AMPHIBOLIC INTERMEDIATES

stem: Which agent is used in the management of cancer?
rationale: Compounds that inhibit the formation of tetrahydrofolates block purine synthesis and have been used in cancer chemotherapy. Azaserine inhibits reaction ⑤ in Figure 33–2.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > INOSINE MONOPHOSPHATE (IMP) IS SYNTHESIZED FROM AMPHIBOLIC INTERMEDIATES > Antifolate Drugs & Glutamine Analogs Block Purine Nucleotide Biosynthesis

stem: Adenine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phosphoryl transfer from PRPP catalyzed by adenosine- and hypoxanthine-phosphoribosyl transferases converts adenine, hypoxanthine, and guanine to their mononucleotides (Figure 33–4).
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > "SALVAGE REACTIONS" CONVERT PURINES & THEIR NUCLEOSIDES TO MONONUCLEOTIDES

stem: Hypoxanthine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phosphoryl transfer from PRPP catalyzed by adenosine- and hypoxanthine-phosphoribosyl transferases converts adenine, hypoxanthine, and guanine to their mononucleotides (Figure 33–4).
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > "SALVAGE REACTIONS" CONVERT PURINES & THEIR NUCLEOSIDES TO MONONUCLEOTIDES

stem: Guanine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phosphoryl transfer from PRPP catalyzed by adenosine- and hypoxanthine-phosphoribosyl transferases converts adenine, hypoxanthine, and guanine to their mononucleotides (Figure 33–4).
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > "SALVAGE REACTIONS" CONVERT PURINES & THEIR NUCLEOSIDES TO MONONUCLEOTIDES

stem: Adenosine kinase acts on which substrate?
rationale: Phosphorylation of the purine nucleotides, catalyzed by adenosine kinase, converts adenosine and deoxyadenosine to AMP and dAMP.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > "SALVAGE REACTIONS" CONVERT PURINES & THEIR NUCLEOSIDES TO MONONUCLEOTIDES

stem: Adenosine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Adenosine is first converted to inosine by adenosine deaminase, EC 3.5.4.4.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > HUMANS CATABOLIZE PURINES TO URIC ACID

stem: Deoxyadenosine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phosphorylation of the purine nucleotides, catalyzed by adenosine kinase, converts adenosine and deoxyadenosine to AMP and dAMP.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > "SALVAGE REACTIONS" CONVERT PURINES & THEIR NUCLEOSIDES TO MONONUCLEOTIDES

stem: Which substance is synthesized by the liver?
rationale: Liver is the major site of purine nucleotide biosynthesis and provides purines and purine nucleosides for salvage and for utilization by tissues incapable of their biosynthesis.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > "SALVAGE REACTIONS" CONVERT PURINES & THEIR NUCLEOSIDES TO MONONUCLEOTIDES

stem: What substance do erythrocytes require for nucleotide formation?
rationale: Erythrocytes and polymorphonuclear leukocytes cannot synthesize 5-phosphoribosylamine and therefore also utilize exogenous purines to form nucleotides.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > "SALVAGE REACTIONS" CONVERT PURINES & THEIR NUCLEOSIDES TO MONONUCLEOTIDES

stem: What substance do polymorphonuclear leukocytes require for nucleotide formation?
rationale: Erythrocytes and polymorphonuclear leukocytes cannot synthesize 5-phosphoribosylamine and therefore also utilize exogenous purines to form nucleotides.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > "SALVAGE REACTIONS" CONVERT PURINES & THEIR NUCLEOSIDES TO MONONUCLEOTIDES

stem: What is the substrate acted upon by ribonucleotide reductase?
rationale: Reduction of the 2'-hydroxyl of purine and pyrimidine ribonucleotides is catalyzed by ribonucleotide reductase, EC 1.17.4.1 (Figure 33–7).
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > REDUCTION OF RIBONUCLEOSIDE DIPHOSPHATES FORMS DEOXYRIBONUCLEOSIDE DIPHOSPHATES

stem: What substance is formed from ribonucleoside diphosphates?
rationale: Reduction of the 2'-hydroxyl of purine and pyrimidine ribonucleotides forms deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates (dNDPs).
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > REDUCTION OF RIBONUCLEOSIDE DIPHOSPHATES FORMS DEOXYRIBONUCLEOSIDE DIPHOSPHATES

stem: What substance are nucleoside diphosphates (NDPs) converted into?
rationale: The conversion of both pyrimidine and purine nucleotides NDPs to NTPs is also feedback inhibited by purine and pyrimidine nucleotides (Figure 33-10).
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > THE DEOXYRIBONUCLEOSIDES OF URACIL & CYTOSINE ARE SALVAGED > Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotide Biosynthesis are Coordinately Regulated

stem: What substance is ribose 5-phosphate converted into?
rationale: Hypoxanthine and PRPP react to form IMP and PPi.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > THE DEOXYRIBONUCLEOSIDES OF URACIL & CYTOSINE ARE SALVAGED

stem: What substance is required by thymidylate synthase?
rationale: The reaction catalyzed by thymidylate synthase, EC 2.1.1.45, is the only reaction of pyrimidine nucleotide biosynthesis that requires a tetrahydrofolate derivative. Dihydrofolate is the oxidized form of tetrahydrofolate.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > THE DEOXYRIBONUCLEOSIDES OF URACIL & CYTOSINE ARE SALVAGED > Methotrexate Blocks Reduction of Dihydrofolate

stem: Which agent is used in the management of gout?
rationale: Allopurinol is used to treat gout.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > THE DEOXYRIBONUCLEOSIDES OF URACIL & CYTOSINE ARE SALVAGED > Certain Pyrimidine Analogs are Substrates for Enzymes of Pyrimidine Nucleotide Biosynthesis

stem: What substance is allopurinol converted into?
rationale: Allopurinol is converted to a nucleotide.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > THE DEOXYRIBONUCLEOSIDES OF URACIL & CYTOSINE ARE SALVAGED > Certain Pyrimidine Analogs are Substrates for Enzymes of Pyrimidine Nucleotide Biosynthesis

stem: Guanosine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Humans convert adenosine and guanosine to uric acid (Figure 33--11).
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > HUMANS CATABOLIZE PURINES TO URIC ACID

stem: Uricase acts on which substrate?
rationale: In mammals other than higher primates, uricase (EC 1.7.3.3) converts uric acid to the water-soluble product allantoin.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > HUMANS CATABOLIZE PURINES TO URIC ACID

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of gout?
rationale: Genetic defects in PRPP synthetase can present clinically as gout.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > DISORDERS OF PURINE METABOLISM

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of gouty arthritis?
rationale: Sodium urate crystals cause an inflammatory reaction known as gouty arthritis.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > DISORDERS OF PURINE METABOLISM

stem: Uric acid lithiasis can develop as a complication of which condition?
rationale: The Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is characterized by frequent episodes of uric acid lithiasis and a bizarre syndrome of self-mutilation.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > DISORDERS OF PURINE METABOLISM > Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome

stem: Self-mutilation can develop as a complication of which condition?
rationale: The Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is characterized by frequent episodes of uric acid lithiasis and a bizarre syndrome of self-mutilation.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > DISORDERS OF PURINE METABOLISM > Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of von Gierke disease?
rationale: von Gierke disease involves purine overproduction and hyperuricemia.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > DISORDERS OF PURINE METABOLISM > von Gierke Disease

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of a deficiency?
rationale: A deficiency in xanthine oxidase can be due to severe liver damage.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > DISORDERS OF PURINE METABOLISM > Hypouricemia

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of aciduria?
rationale: Type II orotic aciduria is due to a deficiency only of orotidylate decarboxylase.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > OVERPRODUCTION OF PYRIMIDINE CATABOLITES > Orotic Aciduria

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of orotic aciduria?
rationale: The deficiency in liver mitochondrial ornithine transcarbamoylase results in mild orotic aciduria.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > OVERPRODUCTION OF PYRIMIDINE CATABOLITES > Deficiency of a Urea Cycle Enzyme Results in Excretion of Pyrimidine Precursors

stem: In which structure is the apical membrane found?
rationale: Two of these encoded proteins are localized to the apical membrane of proximal tubular cells.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides > OVERPRODUCTION OF PYRIMIDINE CATABOLITES > Drugs May Precipitate Orotic Aciduria

stem: IMP is converted into which substance?
rationale: IMP is a precursor both of AMP and GMP. Glutamine provides the 2-amino group of GMP, and aspartate the 6-amino group of AMP.
citation: chapter_33_metabolism_of_purine_and_pyrimidine_nucleotides — Metabolism of Purine & Pyrimidine Nucleotides
